meta.title: Buka Workflows
meta.description: Orchestrator-preset workflows in format 3. The shipped workflow-orchestrator preset (only it can see the creation/start tools) turns a one-off request into a node graph and runs it: each robot keeps one session for the whole run in its workspace under the normal worker preset, compacting that session's history before every later entry. A user node is a user-intervention entry point: the graph pauses and hands the human one of three things only a person can do - wait for a decision, wait for the user to complete a manual action, or wait for feedback on a result only a human can see. A user node has a required title, an optional templated detail shown to the user, outgoing edges that are the user's choices (each with a route name, a user-facing label and an optional description) and optional questions that collect extra answers; the answers feed later prompts as nodes.<id>.route, nodes.<id>.answers.<qid>.selected / .custom and nodes.<id>.text. Definitions containing user nodes run in the foreground with an active caller turn because the native question card needs one (a host restart interrupts such runs); runs without user nodes return the run id as soon as the first node is dispatched and a host-side supervisor keeps scheduling sessions from session events (it never awaits the session result). Robots are normal sessions (runtime roots under the normal approval policy): they can request tool approvals or ask the user questions, and the run page shows a pending-interaction notice with an open-session action; the workflow injects only the task, the declared result contract and the path meanings. Every robot node session also gets four read-only observation tools available when its recorded session id belongs to a run: buka_workflow_overview (compact graph, node summaries/states and the ordered execution list without prompts or final texts), buka_workflow_execution_input and buka_workflow_execution_output (one execution's exact input or recorded output plus its attachment manifest), and buka_workflow_execution_attachment (list or read one attachment in bounded chunks). Attachments are a built-in capability of every robot node for independent data/files (binaries, archives, traces, large datasets), not a channel for the answer itself: a node may return an optional attachments array of workspace-relative paths, the observer copies those files into the execution's node directory, and later prompts can inline small text files or reference them by path. Visibility is rebuilt from run records, so the tools remain available after the run ends or DSH restarts when the robot session is reopened. Releasing a node's live agent re-announces its still-persisted session to clients, so it stays in the sidebar and the page's open-session action keeps working (it refreshes a stale client session list first). A robot node may also set "mode": "plan": its session enters DSH plan mode before the prompt, the robot presents its plan through the native plan review card, and after the user approves it carries out the plan and returns the node result; this is one node, not a separate approval node, and the run page shows a waiting notice while the review is open. Every robot node must declare output, a JSON Schema object for its result JSON; the engine merges next, the built-in abort escape and the built-in attachments capability into the scoped structured_output tool (plain-text JSON is accepted and validated the same way) and validates edge-prompt template variables against the declared schemas at plan time. When the node has outgoing edges, the JSON must carry exactly one of next and abort: next is one of those edge names, or a non-empty list of them to fan out into concurrent branches; the supervisor follows next and its prompt automatically - no when condition and no extra judge agent. A terminal robot node still returns JSON but no next. A valid abort ends the run as failed with the node's reason, follows no edge, and does not require the declared output fields; malformed or ambiguous next/abort results are retried in the same session. Edges on robot nodes are { to, name, prompt }: name is the unique route key, prompt explains that entry's task and what each next value means; report and when are validation errors. A user node's edges are { to, name, label, description?, prompt? }: label is the user-facing option text, prompt is required only when the target is a robot node and forbidden otherwise. There is no default node timeout (an explicit robot timeoutMs is the only hard deadline), interrupted sessions are resumed in the same session; if that fails the run fails with an explicit error and never opens a substitute session, and unfinished runs resume after a host restart except runs that contain user nodes (their question card cannot be recreated). Runs are one-off and format 3 only: a gate node is rejected with a migration error, on startup old-version runs are purged, run numbering restarts at #1 and settings.json keeps the archive settings. A read-only sidebar page draws each persisted run as a vertical git-like graph of capsules with nested side lanes that never cross, mid-path arrows, ×N revisits and gray unreached nodes; robot capsules show the robot's preset avatar and the creator-written step summary, user capsules show their title, the detail panel shows the node's single robot session with an open-session action, and one tab per execution shows the rendered task, the final text, status, time, duration and the route it took (a user execution shows the rendered instruction, the readable answer text and the chosen label), plus a pending-interaction notice, a waiting-for-you notice with an open-session action while a user node is waiting, and recovered/timed-out tags; the output tab shows the final text and attachment downloads, never the raw JSON or key/value routing fields. Every run is numbered in creation order (#N); the page's auto-archive settings archive runs after 24 hours and delete them after 168 hours by default.
